one_line: Agent-assisted theatre discovery with human-controlled booking.
what_it_does: Searches live West End listings and availability, updates the visible storefront/calendar, then leaves checkout to the person.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP shares live catalog and calendar state with the agent and page, preventing guessed listings and keeping payment human-controlled; ordinary UI driving is markedly less reliable.
leverage_evidence: About describes search_events, get_availability, and in-page calendar/listing actuation.
Video frames show ticket listings and date/booking states.
execution_rationale: A coherent live storefront extension with a clearly bounded discovery-to-human-checkout flow; the video shows product states, though no transcript or explicit tool log is available.
execution_evidence: Live demo reported alive and implementation details identify client registration and page bridge.
Frame sheets show event listing and booking UI progression.
impact_rationale: Useful for people trying to find viable theatre dates while preserving trust at purchase; the audience is specific and the solution directly addresses discovery friction.
impact_evidence: Pitch and story describe real ticket discovery and availability use case.
Video shows theatre listing/date-selection workflow.
creativity_rationale: Strong human-agent handoff and shared-page design applied to ticketing, with thoughtful safety boundaries, though the underlying booking category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Agent hunts while human confirms and pays.
Checkout/cart/account navigation is explicitly blocked.
usability_note: Familiar storefront with a simple agent-search then human-book pattern.
red_flags: Video does not clearly expose explicit tool-call trace.
Existing storefront was extended rather than built greenfield.
standouts: WebMCP writes back into the page the buyer is viewing.
advance_reason: High-quality, credible live-product integration with strong leverage and impact.

one_line: A structured visual editor keeping screen specs and wireframes synchronized.
what_it_does: Builds semantic screen blueprints containing layout, states, behaviors, and API mappings, editable by humans and agents.
leverage_rationale: Agents edit the same structured model as the visual editor, preserving relationships that a general agent would have to infer and update through brittle UI actions.
leverage_evidence: Story defines named typed WebMCP editing capabilities on the live blueprint.
Frames show editor panels, blueprint content, and updated screen representations.
execution_rationale: The product presents a coherent editor and AI-proposal workflow with visible screens and structured artifacts; end-to-end approval details are somewhat limited in the frames.
execution_evidence: Public repo and alive demo reported.
Frame sheets show a functioning visual editor and generated/updated layouts.
impact_rationale: Addresses a real cross-functional problem for product/design teams: keeping visual and textual specifications aligned.
impact_evidence: Story identifies maintenance gap between wireframes, states, interactions, and API mappings.
Visible editor supports screen-spec workflow.
creativity_rationale: The blueprint-as-single-structured-model interaction is a fresh synthesis of design editing and agent collaboration.
creativity_evidence: Wireframe and specification are two views of one model.
Human visual judgment and agent structural editing are deliberately separated.
usability_note: Visual canvas plus structured panels makes a complex specification approachable.
red_flags: Explicit agent invocation is not legible in the frame sheets.
standouts: AI proposals are reviewable rather than silently applied.
advance_reason: Strong product concept with credible execution evidence and clear WebMCP value.

one_line: A release-security lab where agents investigate but a deterministic gatekeeper controls approval.
what_it_does: Lets agents test release authority boundaries, find counterexamples, propose remediation, and request verification without self-authorizing release.
leverage_rationale: The agent operates against explicit typed security capabilities while authority remains a separate deterministic state; this shared capability boundary is difficult to replicate reliably through DOM automation.
leverage_evidence: Story describes bounded attack, inspection, remediation, and verification tools.
Frames show dark security/release workflow, logs, and status outputs.
execution_rationale: Ambitious security workflow is coherent and visibly produces evidence/status states, though the full end-to-end path is not transcript-supported.
execution_evidence: Video frames show product console, checks/logs, and resulting release state.
About specifies Gatekeeper, counterexample, rebuild, and fresh verification flow.
impact_rationale: Release teams have a real need for useful agent assistance without delegating final security authority.
impact_evidence: Concrete release-approval threat model and attack cases are described.
Visible security/release status interface.
creativity_rationale: The agent-acts/Gatekeeper-decides/human-verifies interaction is a memorable and deeply pursued safety concept.
creativity_evidence: Separates investigation power from release authority.
Includes adversarial attempts and independent oracle comparison.
usability_note: Technically dense but the staged security lab appears designed to make authority boundaries inspectable.
standouts: Agent cannot approve its own remediation or release.
advance_reason: One of the strongest WebMCP-native concepts, with high leverage, creativity, and credible evidence.

one_line: Local confidential-document analysis with identity-preserving redaction.
what_it_does: Parses documents locally, lets an agent analyze stable tokens instead of identities, and decodes approved answers in the user’s tab.
leverage_rationale: In-page tools enforce a privacy boundary while retaining document structure and stable references; ordinary UI automation cannot safely provide the same guarantee.
leverage_evidence: Story specifies five local WebMCP tools and per-value disclosure policies.
Frames show document analysis and generated response states.
execution_rationale: The privacy-preserving workflow is unusually specific and visibly demonstrated, though the transcript is only music and no public repo is available.
execution_evidence: Demo alive; frame sheets show document UI and analysis output.
Description covers parse, redact/tokenize, analyze, and decode workflow.
impact_rationale: Directly addresses a serious need for useful AI analysis of contracts, patient records, and deals that cannot be shared with an agent in raw form.
impact_evidence: Concrete confidential-document audiences and examples.
Stable token mechanism preserves analytical relationships.
creativity_rationale: Separating structural substance from identity, with reversible user-controlled tokens, is a novel and memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Names become stable tokens while bank details can be withheld entirely.
Decode occurs locally from a user-held key.
usability_note: Per-value/per-type controls and local decode provide a clear privacy-aware workflow.
red_flags: No public repository and explicit tool calls are only partially legible.
advance_reason: High-impact, highly original privacy architecture with visible product evidence.

one_line: A capability surface that follows a human’s current release authorization.
what_it_does: Adds a release tool only for the exact currently approved snapshot, and removes/rejects it after correction, revocation, or stale state.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the security mechanism: human authority changes what the agent can discover, not merely what a permanent handler later denies.
leverage_evidence: Story gives explicit 3-tools → approval → 4-tools → correction/revocation → 3-tools sequence.
Frames show authority/capability UI, invocation, and changed status.
execution_rationale: The central state transition and execution-time revalidation are clearly specified and visibly packaged as a focused proof.
execution_evidence: Alive demo and public repo reported.
Video frames show authorization workflow and resulting capability state.
Description states controlled action records a receipt and revalidates authority.
impact_rationale: Provides a credible pattern for consequential agent actions in release and operations workflows where human authority must remain current.
impact_evidence: Concrete release-manager scenario.
Fail-closed stale-discovery behavior is explicit.
creativity_rationale: Projects authorization as a dynamic browser capability surface, a precise and original use of WebMCP semantics.
creativity_evidence: Consequential tool appears/disappears with human decision.
Human-only grant/revoke/correct controls prevent self-authority.
usability_note: The human/agent action split and next-step visibility make a subtle security flow understandable.
red_flags: External side effects are deliberately simulated, not a real deployment.
standouts: Most direct demonstration of WebMCP changing agent authority.
advance_reason: Outstanding WebMCP leverage and strong focused execution.

one_line: An agent receptionist for a small plumbing business.
what_it_does: Checks service area, availability, pricing, and services, then holds a requested appointment for owner confirmation by text.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools let an agent reliably perform receptionist work on a small business’s existing site and share booking state, while confirmation preserves owner control.
leverage_evidence: Five concrete tools cover area, schedule, estimate, services, and booking.
Frames show front-desk UI and resulting request/response state.
execution_rationale: The scope is focused and the demonstrated workflow has a clear stop at owner confirmation; packaging and live demo are strong.
execution_evidence: Alive demo, public repo, and five gallery images reported.
Video shows customer-facing workflow and updated front-desk state.
impact_rationale: Directly serves an underserved long-tail audience of tiny service businesses that cannot build agent integrations or staff a receptionist.
impact_evidence: Specific three-person plumbing-shop scenario.
Owner confirmation by text addresses real operational constraints.
creativity_rationale: A practical and compelling reframing of a local business website as an agent receptionist, with a safe human handoff.
creativity_evidence: Uses the existing website rather than requiring another dashboard.
Booking is held until owner replies YES.
usability_note: Simple customer request flow and familiar owner confirmation channel.
advance_reason: High impact and practical WebMCP integration for an audience usually left behind.

one_line: A local data viewer where agents and people share a SQL workspace.
what_it_does: Loads local tabular files, exposes schema/query/error/result context to WebMCP agents, and keeps query results in reusable browser tabs.
leverage_rationale: Agents can inspect and modify the full live query context and verify results in place, reducing copy-paste and improving precision beyond generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Story identifies access to query, schema, errors, and results through WebMCP.
Frames clearly show query editor, execution, and result tables.
execution_rationale: A coherent, visibly functional data-analysis product with multiple useful surfaces; completeness beyond the shown workflow is not fully evidenced.
execution_evidence: Alive demo, public repo, and four gallery images.
Video shows SQL/query interaction and resulting data output.
impact_rationale: Makes advanced local data analysis more approachable while retaining power for users who need SQL, including difficult formats such as Parquet.
impact_evidence: Specific pains around SQL expertise and fragmented AI context.
Visible familiar table and results interface.
creativity_rationale: A strong synthesis of spreadsheet familiarity, SQL power, and agent collaboration, though the category is established.
creativity_evidence: Reusable query/result tabs and shared workspace.
Agent can explain, edit, and verify queries in context.
usability_note: Familiar table UI lowers the barrier to complex local analysis.
standouts: Good balance of approachable UI and expert capability.
advance_reason: Credible, useful data workflow with clearly demonstrated agent leverage.

one_line: A browser desktop where humans and agents use shared apps and filesystem.
what_it_does: Provides documents, spreadsheets, canvas, terminal, files, tasks, and project handoffs in a persistent browser workspace exposed through many WebMCP tools.
leverage_rationale: Shared filesystem and application services let an agent perform multi-app work in the same state as the human; generic UI driving would be fragile and difficult to compose.
leverage_evidence: Story describes 89 tools and shared app services/filesystem.
Frames show desktop-like multi-app environment, terminal, documents, and resulting artifacts.
execution_rationale: Very broad scope is coherently presented through a concrete release-planning scenario, with visible multi-app progression; breadth creates some unverified edges.
execution_evidence: Alive demo, public repo, and gallery images reported.
Video shows multiple applications and completed/changed work states.
impact_rationale: Could materially help users and agents coordinate ordinary knowledge work without context switching or handoff loss.
impact_evidence: Specific workflow spans notes, spreadsheet, release brief, PDF, tasks, and canvas.
Persistence and shared filesystem address real workflow friction.
creativity_rationale: The virtual browser operating system and side-by-side human/agent workspace is ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Apps share one filesystem and can be chained.
Projects preserve questions and later-session handoffs.
usability_note: Powerful unified workspace, though 89 tools and many apps imply a substantial learning surface.
red_flags: Very broad scope makes full completeness difficult to verify from one scenario.
standouts: Multi-app shared state is a strong WebMCP fit.
advance_reason: Highly ambitious and clearly demonstrated shared agent workspace.

one_line: ForgeTwin turns natural-language engineering goals into simulated, testable 3D machines.
what_it_does: Builds editable mechanical graphs, runs physics, inspects telemetry and failures, and iterates designs against measurable constraints through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: Typed state-aware tools expose engineering graph construction, simulation, telemetry, and optimization; the agent can iteratively engineer in a shared workspace rather than merely generate text or drive pixels.
leverage_evidence: Story lists 29 granular tools and shared graph used by UI, simulator, and agent.
Frames show 3D engineering workspace, telemetry/technical panels, and resulting design state.
execution_rationale: Exceptionally ambitious and detailed concept with a visible technical product and deterministic fallback, but full physics/design loop is only partially evidenced in frames.
execution_evidence: Alive demo and 13 gallery images reported.
Description specifies versioning, validation, Rapier simulation, telemetry, failure replay, and export.
Video shows 3D product UI and technical outputs.
impact_rationale: Addresses a substantial engineering bottleneck by making simulation-guided concept validation accessible through natural language while explicitly disclaiming certified use.
impact_evidence: Concrete machine examples and measurable constraints.
Physics evidence and failure-driven redesign are central to the product.
creativity_rationale: A highly original and unusually ambitious interaction model: an agent builds, simulates, diagnoses, and redesigns physical systems in an editable engineering world.
creativity_evidence: 39-part vocabulary across many machine families.
Combines structured engineering graph, 3D editing, physics, telemetry, and iterative optimization.
usability_note: Natural-language entry and visual editing are promising, but engineering complexity remains high.
red_flags: Hosted AI/API-key paths and advanced engineering claims are only partially verifiable from the frame sheets.
Not a replacement for certified engineering analysis.
standouts: Most ambitious technical concept in the packet.
Physics-and-evidence framing avoids pure generative 3D claims.
advance_reason: Exceptional creativity and high potential impact, with substantial visible product evidence despite broad scope.

one_line: A live architecture canvas where humans and agents co-edit structured graphs.
what_it_does: Lets an agent build, mutate, lay out, validate, annotate, diff, and export architecture diagrams while humans approve structural changes.
leverage_rationale: Structured graph tools and shared live state are substantially more reliable than dumping Mermaid or scraping a canvas, while approval protects human intent.
leverage_evidence: Story describes 13 typed tools operating on graph semantics.
Frames show architecture canvas, structured nodes, logs, and resulting diagram.
execution_rationale: Focused product is coherently demonstrated with graph source of truth, approval modal, activity log, validation, and export; live demo and repo support completion.
execution_evidence: Alive demo, public repo, and six gallery images reported.
Frame sheets show canvas, invocation/log views, and completed architecture state.
Story specifies React Flow/Zustand/Ajv/Dagre implementation and atomic operations.
impact_rationale: Architecture teams have a real need to create and maintain diagrams collaboratively, and the product directly reduces agent/human representation mismatch.
impact_evidence: Specific engineer workflow and Mermaid export.
Shared graph supports co-editing and validation.
creativity_rationale: A fresh, well-scoped interaction model for agent-assisted diagramming centered on graph semantics rather than pixels.
creativity_evidence: Human approval for structural changes and live co-editing.
Diff, validation, annotation, auto-layout, and export are integrated.
usability_note: Canvas plus approval and activity-log affordances make agent changes inspectable.
standouts: Strong evidence of a complete focused workflow.
advance_reason: Well-executed, high-leverage collaborative canvas with strong evidence.
